result.question: I'd rather take Transformer 1 at site MAIN out of service once than three times. Pull every open and pending-approval work order on it. For each one, give me the number, description, priority and scheduled date, and say whether it needs the unit de-energized, for example internal inspection, OLTC work or electrical testing, or whether it can be done live, for example oil sampling. Group the outage-needing work orders into bundles. Each bundle must have at least two work orders whose scheduled dates fall within 14 days of each other. For each bundle, propose a single outage date where the MAIN calendar has the fewest other scheduled work orders. Estimate each bundle's total planned hours, using the planned hours on the work orders themselves. Where a work order has no plan, use the average actual hours of closed work orders on Transformer 1. Then check the latest acetylene and hydrogen. If acetylene is above 1 ppm, any bundle with OLTC or inspection work moves to the earliest possible date regardless of calendar load. If fewer than two outage-needing work orders exist, don't bundle anything. Recommend whether each one should be done alone or deferred to the next planned outage, and why.

# Transformer 1 @ MAIN — Open & Pending-Approval Work Orders

**Latest DGA (2024-01-19): acetylene 7 ppm, hydrogen 2,850 ppm.** Acetylene is above 1 ppm, so any bundle with OLTC or inspection work goes to the **earliest possible date regardless of calendar load**.

## Work orders

| WO # | Description | Priority | Scheduled date | Live / Outage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection (suspected contact wear/coking) | 1 | 2024-01-19 | **Outage** – OLTC work |
| OUTAGE-T1-COND4 | Priority 1 outage & inspection, IEEE C57.104 Condition 4 (TDCG 32,409 ppm) | 1 | 2024-01-19 | **Outage** – internal inspection |
| DGA-T1-MONTHLY | Monthly DGA resample (due 2024-02-18) | 3 | 2024-02-18 | Live – oil sampling |
| 1000052 | Oil sample retest & insulation check (T3 thermal fault) | 3 | 2024-01-19 (planned labor) | Oil sampling is live; the *insulation check* portion is typically electrical testing — do it during the outage |

## Bundling

Two outage-needing work orders exist (1000051, OUTAGE-T1-COND4), so bundling is permitted. Both are scheduled for 2024-01-19 — well within 14 days of each other.

**Bundle A: {1000051, OUTAGE-T1-COND4} + the insulation-check portion of 1000052**

- **Proposed outage date:** 2024-01-19. Normally I would pick the date with fewest other scheduled WOs on the MAIN calendar — the calendar shows **0 scheduled WOs** in the surrounding window, so 2024-01-19 was already the lightest. But more importantly, since acetylene is 7 ppm (> 1 ppm), this bundle (OLTC + inspection work) moves to the **earliest possible date regardless of calendar load** — which is 2024-01-19.
- **Total planned hours: 8 hours.** Only 1000052 has planned hours (8 h, ELECTECH1, 2024-01-19). 1000051 and OUTAGE-T1-COND4 have no labor plan; the fallback average actual hours of closed Transformer 1 work orders cannot be used because **there are no closed work orders on Transformer 1**. Treat the 8-hour figure as a floor; a Condition 4 internal inspection plus OLTC teardown will realistically exceed one shift — recommend planning multi-day cover (the outage WO itself describes a 2-day window, 2024-01-19 to 2024-01-20).

## Recommendation per work order

- **1000051 (OLTC inspection) — do now, in the Bundle A outage.** Acetylene at 7 ppm indicates arcing/thermal faulting in the OLTC range; with the unit already Condition 4, deferring risks an unplanned failure. Do not defer.
- **OUTAGE-T1-COND4 (Condition 4 outage/inspection) — do now, in the same outage.** TDCG of 32,409 ppm with hydrogen of 2,850 ppm is a severe condition; this is the anchor of the outage.
- **1000052 (oil retest & insulation check) — split it.** Take the oil sample live (can be done immediately), and fold the insulation check into the Bundle A outage so no separate de-energization is needed.
- **DGA-T1-MONTHLY — do live, do not bundle.** Oil sampling requires no outage. Execute it as scheduled on 2024-02-18 (or earlier if the outage findings warrant tightening the cadence), on its own — no reason to hold the unit for it.

**Net result: one outage on 2024-01-19 covers all de-energization work; the monthly resample stays a live, standalone task.**
